methods.label: Arrival-order FIFO
methods.description: Arrival time, then job ID. First waiting model cohorts for equipment exchange.

methods.label: Capacity + longest remaining work
methods.description: Maximum offered station capacity; arrived jobs before future jobs, then longest remaining process work. Exchange after active-model demand clears; challenge staging uses first waiting cohorts.

methods.label: Bottleneck / travel + downstream-first
methods.description: Bottleneck and weighted travel proxy for placement; max-pressure equipment cohorts with a switching penalty; arrived jobs then downstream remaining work. No simulator rollout.

methods.label: GPT-6 Luna (medium)
methods.description: Fresh model decisions on the shared public observation and layout candidates.

methods.label: Jev 1.14.0
methods.description: Pinned Jev typed layout choice and per-job priority scores.

scenarios.name: One station, maximum throughput
scenarios.purpose: Single-device saturation; priority cannot invent parallel capacity.

scenarios.name: Cramped room with external equipment exchange
scenarios.purpose: Two immutable owned instruments, one active position; drain, remove and insert through a checked doorway.

scenarios.name: 32 arms operating in a spacious hall
scenarios.purpose: Prepared samples are initially staged in finite local arm buffers (setup assumption). Exercise dozens of simultaneous arm loads/unloads and device processes, with shared AMRs retained.

scenarios.name: 48 staggered synthesis jobs
scenarios.purpose: Overlapping full extracted workflows, future arrivals and priority updates.

scenarios.name: Three waves of competing demand
scenarios.purpose: Bursts change the bottleneck and compete for transport.

scenarios.name: Long drying overlaps incoming short jobs
scenarios.purpose: Overnight drying uses an explicit 12-hour assumption; no shortening to favor a controller.

scenarios.name: Transport-limited short operations
scenarios.purpose: One AMR serves dispersed arms; device capacity alone does not determine completion time.

scenarios.name: Admission and finite buffer pressure
scenarios.purpose: Multi-step jobs reserve future buffer credits, exposing admission and handoff pressure.

scenarios.name: Matched workload in a compact room
scenarios.purpose: Paired with scenario 10; room shape changes placement and travel while jobs/count limits remain identical.

scenarios.name: Matched workload in a wide room
scenarios.purpose: Paired with scenario 09; neither monotone performance nor an optimum is assumed.

scenarios.name: Start downstream chains before the short queue
scenarios.purpose: Same initial layout can be held fixed to isolate FIFO versus downstream-aware job ordering; source process windows unchanged.

scenarios.name: Thirty-six owned instruments, two room bays
scenarios.purpose: Owned device bodies alone exceed room floor area (36 x 0.72 x 0.58 > 4 x 3.4 m2). Fixed 36-device inventory; one or two active bays, others outside. Choose model pairs and exchange timing.

scenarios.name: Upcoming waves compete with present demand
scenarios.purpose: Choose between draining short current work, a long process cohort and upcoming demand; repeated exchanges incur actual handling and movement time.

scenarios.name: Pack the active work near intake instead of filling the hall
scenarios.purpose: Identical geometry validation and bodies; compare spread, tightly packed and reduced-count cells under one shared AMR. Free area need not become transport distance.

scenarios.name: Synthetic screening in a 14 × 10 m room
scenarios.purpose: Synthetic development fixture. Room and count limits are benchmark assumptions, not measured laboratory requirements. Scheduler development variant: synthetic 900-second job arrivals; separate from fixed 0.2 comparisons.

scenarios.name: Synthetic screening in a 8 × 7 m room
scenarios.purpose: Synthetic development fixture. Room and count limits are benchmark assumptions, not measured laboratory requirements. Scheduler development variant: synthetic 900-second job arrivals; separate from fixed 0.2 comparisons.

model_reruns.reason: Saved answers failed the canonical exact-current-job-set validation. Preserve the failed attempts; rerun fresh inference with local schema/ID validation before writing. No task, engine, budget, candidate or score changes.

conditions.candidate_search: Original cases: capacity/reverse/half. Decision challenges: screened spread/packed/reverse/half or active model multisets; all compared methods receive the same public problem. Custom canonical policy plugins may submit arbitrary layouts in a separately declared track.
source_kind: public LeMat-Synth annotation subset (not gated Hugging Face database dump)

jev.note: Usage-based estimate, not an invoice. Failed requests retain conservative reservations.

failure_payload_note: Initial failed Jev adapter overwrote same-epoch bodies; hashes/status/reservations and last payload survive. Final comparison calls once per epoch; new requests use UUID filenames.
caveats: Fourteen cases use the public LeMat annotation subset, not the gated full database; two scheduler development cases are wholly synthetic. Literature operation times retain source provenance; workload composition, arrivals, geometry and staging are engineering assumptions.

The original ten literature-derived cases retain their restricted three-layout menu. Updated trials are selected after the declared refresh time; earlier trials remain archived. Missing cells represent pending runs.

Two synthetic scheduler development tasks retain their existing task IDs, seeds and workloads. Their one-arm-per-cell menu excludes proposals exceeding the eight-arm ceiling; these are not literature-derived experiments.
New challenge cases compare five policies through the same public observation, candidates, canonical decision and engine. Sophisticated algorithms are valid contestants; no LLM win is assumed.

One selected valid trial per method/scenario version; no statistical ranking or global optimum claim. Malformed-answer attempts are preserved separately. Three Luna cases were rerun from fresh sessions after invalid priority job sets were found; selection follows run time and task/config matching, not score. Missing pairs mean not run, not failure or zero time.

Three Luna conditions have an additional failed formatting attempt. The shared decision cap applies per session; cumulative inference attempts are therefore unequal, and these exploratory results do not establish a statistical model ranking.
Case 03 v2 starts prepared samples in local finite buffers; setup transport is outside its boundary. Intake-fed v1 remains archived.

After the shared 32-decision cap, last priorities persist. Exchange drains admitted whole jobs; workflows requiring all stages cannot span missing-device configurations in this draft. Staging challenges deliberately use independent source-derived unit operations.
Tight packing preserves device dimensions, arm reach, buffers, AMR footprint and route checks. Geometry validity is not articulated robot collision or real laboratory safety certification.
